pages.title: Introduction
pages.description: Action Platform creates projects from templates, enforces git-flow, cuts versioned releases and deploys them to your cloud, from a web app, a CLI or MCP.

pages.title: Why Action Platform
pages.description: Open source and self-hosted, deploys that always ship a tagged release, git-flow enforced in three places, AWS deploys without access keys.

pages.title: Core concepts
pages.description: Organization, team, project, app, template, manifest, git-flow, release, scope, deploy target, deployment, readiness, job and plugin, and how they relate.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: Install the Action Platform CLI, create a project from a template, open a pull request through git-flow and cut a first release in minutes.

pages.title: Templates
pages.description: Project types, stacks and templates, cloud overlays and services, and how an organization adds its own template repositories.

pages.title: Git-flow
pages.description: Branch kinds, base branches, pull request targets and Conventional Commits, enforced by git hooks, CI and branch protection on the code host.

pages.title: Releases
pages.description: How a release is cut: version from LAST_VERSION, release candidates, changelog from Conventional Commits, tag and host release, per component.

pages.title: Scopes
pages.description: Scopes are the named destinations of an app. Their criticality decides which release candidates, stable releases and hotfixes they accept.

pages.title: Deployments
pages.description: Deploy targets and executors, readiness checks, preflight, deploy jobs, verification at the destination, history, rollback and tear-down.

pages.title: Cloud identity
pages.description: The platform as an OpenID Connect issuer: short-lived tokens per app that AWS trusts, so deploys need no stored access keys.

pages.title: Access control
pages.description: Roles, permissions, token scopes and reach in Action Platform, and the commit identity the platform uses.

pages.title: Service access
pages.description: Keep access on GitHub and other services in line with platform roles and teams: audit, grant, revoke, offboard and sync.

pages.title: Observability
pages.description: Instance health, worker heartbeats and Sentry error reporting for the API, web app, CLI and MCP server.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.description: What an Action Platform plugin adds or replaces, its options per organization, the plugin index and how the hosted platform bundles plugins.

pages.title: Project scaffolding
pages.description: Start every service, library or job from the same tested template with tests, lint, CI and deploy files in place.

pages.title: Development standards
pages.description: Enforce one git-flow and Conventional Commits across every repository with git hooks, CI checks and branch protection.

pages.title: Delivery automation
pages.description: From merged work to a versioned release, readiness checks, a deploy and verification at the destination.

pages.title: Self-service deployments
pages.description: Let developers and AI agents deploy within roles, scopes and readiness checks, with no cloud credentials to hand out.

pages.title: Platform engineering
pages.description: Run a self-hosted internal developer platform with your templates, deploy targets, access rules and existing repositories.

pages.title: Deploy from the web
pages.description: Step by step from a fresh Action Platform instance to a verified deployment: code host, app, deploy target, scopes, release, deploy.

pages.title: Deploy to AWS Lambda
pages.description: Connect an AWS account with an IAM-only stack, apply the aws/lambda overlay and deploy web apps without access keys.

pages.title: Add your own templates
pages.description: Register a plain repository or a template catalog with index.json as templates for your organization.

pages.title: Adopting repositories
pages.description: Bring existing repositories onto Action Platform: import, install the platform files, keep their CI, tags and deploy history.

pages.title: Self-hosting
pages.description: Install Action Platform with one command or on Dokploy: services, environment variables, first run, backups and upgrades.

pages.title: Operations
pages.description: Run an Action Platform instance: what holds state, backups, restore into a fresh host, losing and rotating secrets.

pages.title: platform.toml
pages.description: Every table and key of platform.toml: project, source host, release, deploy targets, scopes, services, components and branch protection.

pages.title: CLI
pages.description: Every action-platform command, its flags and the environment variables it reads.

pages.title: Web app
pages.description: Every screen of the Action Platform web app: setup, projects, apps, releases, scopes, deployments, pipelines, connections, team and settings.

pages.title: MCP
pages.description: The Action Platform MCP server for AI agents: local and remote tools, prompts, skills and the rules the server states.

pages.title: API
pages.description: The JSON API behind the Action Platform web app: authentication, routes, jobs, webhooks, readiness and errors.

pages.title: Security
pages.description: How Action Platform authenticates people and programs, seals secrets, verifies webhooks and reaches the cloud without stored keys.

pages.title: Database
pages.description: The Postgres database the API owns: connecting, migrations, adopting an existing schema, tables and the job queue.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: Packages, contexts and layers of Action Platform, how a call passes the gate, how a deploy runs end to end and how credentials travel.

pages.title: Development
pages.description: Run Action Platform locally, run the tests, regenerate the API client, and how this repository releases itself.

pages.title: Writing a plugin
pages.description: Write an Action Platform plugin: the package, the class, providers, options, access providers and the rules of the official index.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: What each message the platform refuses with means and what to do: releases, deploys, git hosts, git-flow, access, self-hosting.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: Short definitions of every Action Platform term, from app and scope to readiness, executor and connected account.
